newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bunge says puzzled by Defiance valuation.
newsitem.headline: Bunge says puzzled by Defiance valuation.

text.p: Latin American-based food group Bunge Corp said on Tuesday the valuation of its takeover target Defiance Mills Ltd was clearly not supported by comparable trading companies or transactions.
Earlier in Defiance's Part B formal response to the Bunge offer, accountancy firm Price Waterhouse said it valued Defiance shares at between A$2.65 and A$2.85 each.
This compared with the Bunge offer of A$1.70 for each Defiance ordinary share.
The most relevant comparable publicly traded companies for Defiance are Goodman Fielder Ltd and George Weston Foods Ltd, Bunge said.

They are universally regarded to be better positioned in the Australian milling and baking industries in terms of competitive position and brand strength and have historically achieved significantly better operating results than Defiance, it said.
It said Goodman and Weston currently trade at an average prospective price/earnings (P/E) multiple of 14.3. Adding a control premium of 25 percent implies a multiple of 17.8.

"The A$2.75 midpoint of the Price Waterhouse valuation implies a 24.9 multiple for Defiance, far in excess of the multiples (inclusive of a control premium) commanded by very comparable and yet better performing companies," Bunge said.

"In evaluating Bunge's offer shareholders should remember that over the year before we announced our offer, Defiance ordinary shares traded at an average price of A$1.23," Bunge chairman Barry Weir said in a statement.
"It is remarkable that shareholders are suddenly expected to believe that the company is worth more than twice the market valuation of only three months ago," Weir said.
The Bunge parent company is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil.
Defiance shares closed five cents up at A$1.95 on 37,864 shares traded.
